title: adaptive-evict-and-index-stitcher-runtime-patch-for-gpu-memory-leak
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Customer escalations observed across Hosted, Dedicated and Private fleets where long-running sessions triggered intermittent GPU OOMs. Investigation shows a combination of aggressive KV cache index fragmentation, stale index pointers after partial compaction, and an eviction race that allowed session handles to remain referenced (a form of leak). This ticket tracks the runtime patch: an adaptive eviction policy, an index-stitcher reconciliation pass, and a conservative per-session soft-reserve to prevent sudden OOM cascades.
comments: 2026-03-10: Initial triage — SRE alerted to a spike in OOMs across hosted bursts. Early signal: tail latencies and token rejections spike before OOMs. Customers A and B reported dedicated node failures; Private deployment C reported similar pattern after sustained long chat sessions.

2026-03-10: Reproduction attempt in staging — synthetic long sessions with prefix-heavy prompts reproduced GPU memory growth and eventual OOM within 2–6 hours. Heap snapshots show large numbers of KV handles not freed; index compaction job logged partial truncation errors.

2026-03-11: Root cause hypothesis — race between asynchronous compaction and eviction threads leaves dangling index entries. When compaction partially fails, the index layout is repaired lazily; eviction assumes stable index and skips handles referenced by the dangling entries, effectively leaking activation-sized allocations.

2026-03-11: Immediate mitigation deployed — lowered per-session cache quota on Hosted and Dedicated by 25% and enabled short-term backpressure on new session allocation to prevent new long-lived sessions from starting. Mitigation reduced OOM occurrence but does not close root cause.

2026-03-12: Proposed fix — (1) adaptive eviction threshold: eviction aggressiveness adapts to active_kv_ratio and recent compaction success rate; (2) index-stitcher: compact-time reconciliation pass that locates stale pointers and stitches or tombstones them deterministically; (3) soft-reserve per session: reserve small headroom to avoid immediate OOM on transient spikes.

2026-03-12: Trade-offs discussed — aggressive eviction reduces tail latency stability and may increase token CPU cost; index-stitcher adds compaction CPU but runs at low priority and can be throttled. Decided to default to conservative settings with opt-in more aggressive profiles for Dedicated customers who request lower cost.

2026-03-13: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4872 — includes index-stitcher implementation and adaptive-evict knobs. Unit tests and fuzz harness added for race scenarios. TODO: load test with production-like traffic and run canary.

2026-03-13: Integration tests — passed extended mem-pressure tests in CI; staging run for 24h showed no unbounded memory growth on synthetic long sessions. Found an edge-case where stitcher held a mutex too long; micro-optimizations committed.

2026-03-14: Canary plan approved — stepwise rollout: (a) small canary on Hosted region us-west-2 (5% traffic) for 48h with aggressive logging; (b) expand to Dedicated pilot (customer sandbox nodes) for 48h; (c) full rollout with feature flag off by default for Private until customer opt-in. Metrics and alert thresholds documented.
2026-03-14: Communication — wrote incident note and customer-facing summary draft. Notified support and account teams of imminent canary and mitigation knobs available if regressions occur.
Next: monitor canary for 72h, collect heap diffs, and prepare postmortem including long-term mitigation scheduling for a lower-overhead compaction algorithm.
deploy_steps: Merge PR after two approvers and green CI: runtime PR #4872
Build runtime image with tag runtime-2026.03-patch1
Deploy to staging cluster and run 48h mem-pressure scenario (automation script: scripts/e2e/mem_stress.sh)
Canary rollout: enable feature-flag 'adaptive-evict-stitcher' for us-west-2 hosted 5% traffic
Monitor: GPU memory tail, kv_active_ratio, compaction_success_rate, eviction_rate via dashboards (dashboard link below)
If stable: expand to Dedicated pilot nodes and then controlled Private customer opt-ins
When safe: flip default config to enabled in runtime-2026.03 release branch and schedule backfill to release notes and changelog
